question: South Carolina Republican Senate Special Primary Winner
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the special Republican Primary for United States Senator from South Carolina, including any potential runoff.

If no 2026 special South Carolina Republican Senate Primary takes place by November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the candidate who is the official Republican nominee to contest the November 3, 2026 South Carolina U.S. Senate election.

If the results of the special primary are not definitively known, or if there is no Republican nominee to contest the November 3, 2026 South Carolina U.S. Senate election, by November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the South Carolina Republican party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
I could only use material published on or before 2026-08-06, so I've left out everything from the August 11 primary onward. On that date the race was still open. Darline Graham Nordone, the appointed senator and Lindsey Graham's sister, was the prediction-market favorite and had Trump's endorsement. Ralph Norman led or was close in the July polls, and a runoff looked likely.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria name the SC Republican Party's first announcement of results, with no URL. Before the vote there were no results to report.
- 2026-07 (filing page): The SC Election Commission's page sets filing for July 21 to July 28 at noon, early voting for August 5 to 7, the special primary for **Tuesday, August 11**, early voting for any runoff for August 19 to 21, and **the runoff, if needed, for Tuesday, August 25**. The primary is held because the Republican nominee died (S.C. Code 7-11-55). Only Republicans can file, and people who voted in the June Democratic primary cannot vote. [SC Votes](https://scvotes.gov/u-s-senate-special-republican-party-filing-primary/)
- If no one gets a majority, the top two go to a runoff, so the question may not be settled until August 25.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing had been settled as of 2026-08-06. Early voting started August 5.
- 2026-07-31: Twelve people filed and the SC GOP decertified three: Danny Ford II, Darius Mitchell and Clark Nielson. Nine remained: Duke Buckner, Russell Fry, Darline Graham, Mark Lynch, Mark McBride, Ralph Norman, Samuel Shepard, Glenda Gail Parker and Mark Sanford. A temporary restraining order kept Ford on the ballot, with a hearing set for August 3. I did not find the result of that hearing. [WBTV](https://www.wbtv.com/2026/07/31/south-carolina-gop-boots-three-candidates-special-primary-legal-battle-underway/)
- Nancy Mace and Joe Wilson are not running. Mace dropped out on July 21 and endorsed Norman. [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/07/22/s-c-succession-second-u-s-senate-poll-shows-ralph-norman-leading/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-05: Five candidates debated on Monday (August 3), including Graham Nordone. The others debated again on Tuesday (August 4) and criticized her for skipping that one. [DeFi Rate](https://defirate.com/news/prediction-markets-favor-graham-nordone-south-carolina-senate/)
- 2026-07-28: AP reports that Trump backed Darline Graham before she announced, though he had earlier suggested he might back Fry. Norman has endorsements from Mace, other House colleagues and law enforcement officials. Lynch is expected to fund his own campaign. The Democratic nominee is Dr. Annie Andrews. [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/south-carolina-republicans-line-up-to-run-in-special-primary-to-replace-late-sen-lindsey-graham)
- 2026-07-21: Mace drops out and endorses Norman. [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/07/22/s-c-succession-second-u-s-senate-poll-shows-ralph-norman-leading/)
- 2026-07-16: Lindsey Graham died on July 11. He had won the June 9 primary with 57% to Lynch's 29%. Gov. McMaster appointed Darline Graham to serve out the term. [Ballotpedia News](https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/07/16/lindsey-grahams-death-will-set-off-a-special-primary-election-for-a-senate-seat-thats-open-for-the-second-time-since-1956/)

## 4. Base rates and polls
- Ballotpedia says this is only the second time the seat has been open since 1956. [Ballotpedia](https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/07/16/lindsey-grahams-death-will-set-off-a-special-primary-election-for-a-senate-seat-thats-open-for-the-second-time-since-1956/)
- I could not find a systematic base rate for appointed senators in special primaries. In this race the DeFi Rate article itself warns that Trump's backing does not guarantee a win, pointing to his joint endorsement of Pamela Evette and Alan Wilson in the governor's race.
- July 20 to 21, Innovative Communication Strategies poll (788 likely voters, ±3.5): Norman 18.6, Graham Nordone 16.3, Fry 11.7, Lynch 8.6, Mace 6.5, Evette 5.6, Sanford 5, undecided 26.3. [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/07/22/s-c-succession-second-u-s-senate-poll-shows-ralph-norman-leading/)
- July 28 to 29, Emerson/Nexstar poll (500 likely GOP voters per the memo, ±4.3; one outlet reported 857): Norman 22, Graham 19, Fry 12, Sanford 11, about 25% undecided. Head-to-head runoff tests: Graham 40, Norman 35; Fry 40, Graham 31. [Emerson](https://emersoncollegepolling.com/south-carolina-2026-poll-no-clear-leader-to-replace-late-sen-graham-on-ballot/), [Mediaite](https://www.mediaite.com/politics/first-poll-on-south-carolina-senate-race-for-lindsey-grahams-seat-shows-runoff-is-likely/)
- Both polls put every candidate well below 50%, so a runoff looked likely.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-05: Kalshi had Graham Nordone at 63% (about $4M traded), Norman at 22% and Fry in the mid-teens. Polymarket had Graham Nordone at 61% (about $400K traded). [DeFi Rate](https://defirate.com/news/prediction-markets-favor-graham-nordone-south-carolina-senate/)
- Early-to-mid July: a Polymarket market on who finishes first in the first round had Graham Nordone at about 71.7%, Norman 15.8% and Fry 5.3%. [PredictionEdge](https://www.predictionedge.com/elections/us-senate/south-carolina-primary-first-place/)
- None of the sources I read before August 6 showed meaningful prices for Mace, Wilson, Lynch or Sanford.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- August 5 to 7: early voting.
- August 11: special primary. If no one wins a majority, the top two advance.
- August 19 to 21: early voting for a runoff. August 25: runoff, which is about when the question resolves.
- Other things that could matter: the court ruling on Ford's ballot spot, any new Trump involvement, endorsements from candidates who are eliminated, and turnout limits caused by the rule against voting after the Democratic primary.

Sources: [SC Votes](https://scvotes.gov/u-s-senate-special-republican-party-filing-primary/), [WBTV](https://www.wbtv.com/2026/07/31/south-carolina-gop-boots-three-candidates-special-primary-legal-battle-underway/), [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/south-carolina-republicans-line-up-to-run-in-special-primary-to-replace-late-sen-lindsey-graham), [Ballotpedia News](https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/07/16/lindsey-grahams-death-will-set-off-a-special-primary-election-for-a-senate-seat-thats-open-for-the-second-time-since-1956/), [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/07/22/s-c-succession-second-u-s-senate-poll-shows-ralph-norman-leading/), [Emerson](https://emersoncollegepolling.com/south-carolina-2026-poll-no-clear-leader-to-replace-late-sen-graham-on-ballot/), [Mediaite](https://www.mediaite.com/politics/first-poll-on-south-carolina-senate-race-for-lindsey-grahams-seat-shows-runoff-is-likely/), [DeFi Rate](https://defirate.com/news/prediction-markets-favor-graham-nordone-south-carolina-senate/), [PredictionEdge](https://www.predictionedge.com/elections/us-senate/south-carolina-primary-first-place/)

forecasts.reasoning:
Carolina GOP primaries and runoffs at a high rate, roughly 75 to 85% in open-seat races.
- Appointed senators running in special primaries usually win, though not always (Luther Strange lost in 2017).
- Candidates who have dropped out, such as Mace and Wilson, almost never win.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-07-28: AP reported Trump's endorsement of Graham Nordone.
- 2026-07-28/29: Emerson poll had Norman 22, Graham 19, Fry 12, Sanford 11, with about 25% undecided. Its runoff tests showed Graham 40 to Norman 35, and Fry 40 to Graham 31.
- 2026-07-20/21: The ICS poll had Norman 18.6 and Graham 16.3.
- 2026-08-05: Markets had Graham Nordone at about 62%, Norman at 22% and Fry in the mid-teens.
- Mace dropped out on July 21 and endorsed Norman.
- Graham Nordone skipped a debate and drew criticism for it.

The polls are softer for Graham Nordone than the market is. In particular, the Fry-versus-Graham runoff test shows she could be vulnerable. I move slightly below the market on her, from about 62% to 55%, and give the difference to Norman and Fry.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** Fry and Norman split the anti-establishment vote, but Fry edges Graham Nordone for second place. He then consolidates Norman and Mace voters in the runoff and wins, as the Emerson head-to-head suggests he could. Alternatively, Sanford's name recognition carries him into a runoff.
